items.title: Home
items.text:
FlashDreams

FlashDreams is an inference and serving runtime for turning world models into live, controllable simulations. FlashDreams runs models in a continuous loop, carrying state forward and streaming frames while new actions or sensor inputs change what happens next step. Whether the application is a game world, an autonomous-vehicle simulator, robotic policy testing, or a virtual training environment, FlashDreams is the runtime to make it possible.

Get Started! GitHub Contribute Explore FlashDreams

Choose a section to get started or browse the project.

Get StartedInstall FlashDreams and run your first model. ModelsBrowse default supported models. DemosExplore our interactive experiences and model interfaces. DocumentationCheckout our CLI, Demo API, Inferencing API, tooling, or related guides. CommunityFind contribution documentation and support channels. Why FlashDreams? Serving World Models is Hard

Building a static clip generator is not enough for world-model serving.

Worlds evolve over time

World models are taught to generate and evolve an environment over time. They support robotics-policy testing, autonomous-vehicle simulation, interactive worlds, and other applications.

Serving has two parts
  1. Inference of a video model that consumes inputs such as clock time and sensors while evolving world state.
  2. A separate application that coordinates inputs, model state, GPU inference, and output.
FlashDreams was built for both parts:
  1. The Inferencing API helps model designers implement stateful world-model inference.
  2. The Demo API helps application developers build experiences around the constraints of world-model serving.
Performance Each tile shows speedup over an existing implementation of the same model. Both run the same weights on the same GPU, so the gain comes from the FlashDreams runtime alone. 2.12× Self-Forcing speedup 3.10× LingBot-World speedup 1.40× Wan2.1 speedup 1.42× FlashVSR speedup

Supported Models Streaming and autoregressive model implementations emit per-step output with sub-second latency once warm; bidirectional model implementations are kept as full-block parity references. Each model page carries the canonical invocation, the checkpoint source, and the per-implementation knobs. OmniDreamsInteractive world simulator for autonomous vehicles. Cosmos3 Nano Sim AutoDriving video with multiple cameras and optional LiDAR. Cosmos3 Nano Sim BimanualController-driven robot-manipulation video. Self-ForcingAutoregressive text-to-video based on Wan 2.1. Causal-ForcingAutoregressive text/image-to-video based on Wan 2.1. Causal Wan 2.2Autoregressive text-to-video based on Wan 2.2 from FastVideo. LingBot-WorldCamera-controllable image-to-video world model. Waypoint 1.5Interactive world model controlled by keyboard and mouse. SANA-WMCamera-controlled world model with streaming and bidirectional variants. FlashVSRStreaming video super-resolution. SwiftVRReal-time streaming video restoration with 2× and 4× presets. Wan 2.1Bidirectional text-to-video and image-to-video generation. Wan 2.2 TI2V-5BBidirectional text-and-image-to-video generation. Cosmos-Predict2.5Bidirectional Text2World, Image2World, and Video2World generation.

items.title: Try FlashDreams!
items.text: The Get Started guide walks from a fresh checkout to running OmniDreams, an interactive driving world-model demo built on FlashDreams.

items.title: Troubleshooting
items.text:
Use this page for common first-run failures before opening an issue. Each entry lists the visible symptom, the most likely cause, and the next concrete step to try.

Current model applications implement flashdreams.api_v2 and run with flashdreams-run-v2. Runtime flags precede --; application flags follow it. Do not move flags across that separator. See the CLI reference for the command shape.

items.title: Launching a Demo Takes a Long Time
items.text:
Symptoms:

  • A demo takes a long time to launch.

Likely cause:

The first run downloads model assets and spends several minutes compiling (and potentially autotuning) kernels.

Fix or next step:

Let the first launch finish if it is still making progress. Subsequent launches reuse compiled kernels and autotuning results, although CUDA graphs are captured again for each process.

items.title: Triton autotuning or warmup looks stuck
items.text:
Symptoms:

  • The first launch takes several minutes.
  • Logs mention Triton autotuning or CUDA-graph warmup.
  • Later runs are much faster than the first run.

Likely cause:

  • Cold runs include one-time setup. The quickstart and model pages document that first launches can include downloads, Triton autotuning, CUDA-graph warmup, native-code compilation, etc...

Fix or next step:

Let the first launch finish if it is still making progress. Subsequent launches reuse compiled kernels and autotuning results, although CUDA graphs are captured again for each process.

Lock file for compilation (pytorch/triton/...) may be tracking a hanging-process. if this is the case, delete the offending lock file and rerun the command.

items.title: CUDA or PyTorch build mismatch
items.text:
Symptoms:

  • A CUDA extension fails to build or load.
  • flashdreams-run-v2 interactive-drive-omnidreams-perf --mode native-window exits instead of falling back to the default PyTorch path.
  • Errors mention nvcc, a CUDA version, a GPU architecture, or missing CUDA libraries.

Likely cause:

The OmniDreams perf application config uses native DiT acceleration with native_dit_acceleration="required". That path requires a source checkout, git, network access for pinned third-party sources, and a CUDA toolchain with nvcc matching the installed PyTorch build. The fast perf variant also uses native FP8 LightVAE. The native kernels are tuned for Blackwell GPUs; use a model-page configuration documented for the installed GPU.

Fix or next step:

Start with the non-perf OmniDreams launch in NVIDIA OmniDreams. The perf application downloads its pinned third-party sources on first use. Verify that the machine has network access, the required GPU, and a CUDA toolchain that matches the PyTorch build before launching:

python -c "import torch; print(torch.__version__, torch.version.cuda)"
nvcc --version

items.title: Disk or cache exhaustion
items.text:
Symptoms:

  • A first run fails while downloading or loading checkpoints.
  • The process reports no space left on device, stops mid-load, or leaves a partial Hugging Face cache.
  • Output video or stats files are missing after an interrupted run.

Likely cause:

Model checkpoints and example assets are cached on first use. LingBot-World downloads a checkpoint of about 70 GB through the Hugging Face cache and its docs recommend keeping about 200 GB free for the model plus cache. Its example data is stored in the FlashDreams user cache under example_data/lingbot_world/<NN>/. Generated MP4s consume space wherever --output-path points.

Fix or next step:

Check free space on both the repository filesystem and the Hugging Face cache filesystem. If the default cache location is too small, point HF_HOME at a larger volume before running the model:

export HF_HOME=/path/to/large/cache

Then rerun the same command so the downloader can reuse or repair the cache.

items.title: Model download or authentication failure
items.text:
Symptoms:

  • A download returns 401, 403, not found, or gated-repository errors.
  • OmniDreams scene or checkpoint downloads fail before the demo starts.
  • LingBot-World fails while fetching the model checkpoint from Hugging Face.

Likely cause:

Most model runs need Hugging Face authentication. OmniDreams requires an HF_TOKEN with read access to the nvidia/omni-dreams-scenes dataset and the nvidia/omni-dreams-models model repository. Other model pages also document first-run downloads from Hugging Face.

Fix or next step:

Export a valid token in the same shell that launches FlashDreams:

export HF_TOKEN=<your-hf-token>

If the token is already set, confirm that the account behind it can open the model or dataset page referenced by the failing command, then rerun the FlashDreams command.

items.title: GPU out of memory
items.text:
Symptoms:

  • The run exits with CUDA out of memory or the Python process is killed during model load or generation.
  • LingBot-World runs out of memory on a single GPU when using large --total-blocks values.
  • Multi-GPU commands fail after one or more ranks report memory pressure.

Likely cause:

The selected model, resolution, rollout length, or GPU count does not fit the available VRAM. The model pages list minimum VRAM expectations: OmniDreams is about 48 GB, Self-Forcing is about 24 GB, and LingBot-World is about 120 GB.

Fix or next step:

Use a smaller documented run first: reduce --total-blocks, lower --pixel-height and --pixel-width where the model supports those runtime overrides, or use the model page's documented multi-GPU torchrun --nproc_per_node=<N> launch. With flashdreams-run-v2, runtime flags go before -- and application flags such as --total-blocks go after it. For LingBot-World, use the efficient streaming application slug cam2v-lingbot-world-fast-taehv-window15-sink3.

items.title: WebRTC connection or video does not appear
items.text:
Symptoms:

  • The URL printed by a WebRTC application is not reachable from the browser.
  • The page loads but video never appears.
  • The server seems idle before printing the connection URL.

Likely cause:

The WebRTC servers open their HTTP port only after model load and warmup. On a remote or cloud GPU instance, the server port may not be reachable directly at the host IP.

Reaching http://<server>:8089/ proves that the HTTP page and signaling path are reachable, but it does not prove that the WebRTC media path is reachable. After signaling, WebRTC still needs a working media path negotiated by ICE. Video uses SRTP, the control data channel uses SCTP over DTLS, and both typically depend on UDP connectivity. Plain SSH -L forwarding, or any other TCP-only forward of the HTTP port, does not forward that WebRTC media path.

If the page loads but video does not appear, ICE may be unable to find a working media path, or the browser may be hiding local IPs in ICE candidates with mDNS hostnames.

Fix or next step:

Wait until the v2 server prints Open http://<server-ip>:8089/ in a browser. For remote machines, forward the documented HTTP port and open the local URL:

ssh -L 8089:localhost:8089 <user>@<host>

Then open http://localhost:8089/.

If the page loads but the video still does not appear, use a setup that carries both the HTTP path and the WebRTC media path:

  • Direct browser access to the server network, with the firewall or security group allowing the WebRTC media traffic advertised during ICE negotiation in addition to the HTTP port.
  • A VPN or UDP-capable forwarding solution between the browser and the server.
  • A TURN relay that you provide and configure when direct peer-to-peer connectivity is blocked. STUN can help ICE discover reachable addresses, but STUN is not a relay. Do not assume a WebRTC demo deploys TURN unless its model page or launch command documents it.

If the media path is available and the connection still fails, check the browser's ICE policy. Some browsers can hide local IP addresses behind mDNS .local hostnames. Disable that behavior and reload:

  • Chrome / Edge: chrome://flags/#enable-webrtc-hide-local-ips-with-mdns set to Disabled, then restart the browser.
  • Brave: brave://settings/privacy/security, set WebRTC IP handling policy to Default public and private interfaces.
  • Firefox: about:config, set media.peerconnection.ice.obfuscate_host_addresses to false.

items.title: Overview
items.text: ContributeDevelopment workflow, testing requirements, and contribution policy. Bugs and feature requestsSearch existing reports or open an issue with a reproducible example. DiscordAsk questions and share results in #flashdreams on the NVIDIA Omniverse server. SecurityFollow the private disclosure process for vulnerabilities.

items.title: Before opening an issue
items.text:
Check Troubleshooting, the model page, and existing issues first. Reduce the problem to the shortest command you can. Include:

  • what you ran and what you expected;
  • the full error text, not a screenshot;
  • FlashDreams, Python, CUDA, and GPU versions; and
  • anything you already tried.

items.title: What hardware do I need?
items.text: FlashDreams needs a recent NVIDIA GPU. Memory requirements depend on the model, so check its model page before installing it.

items.title: Why are integrations not on PyPI?
items.text:
Only the core flashdreams package is published to PyPI. Clone the repository and install an integration as a workspace package. For example:

uv sync --package flashdreams-wan21 --extra dev

items.title: Which Python API should I use?
items.text: Make demos using world-models with our Demo API. Implement world-models with our Inferencing API.

items.title: How do I implement a model with flashdreams?
items.text:
1. Implement a model in FlashDreams, then
  2. Integrate your new model with a demo.

items.title: Overview
items.text:
Demos pair an interactive experience or input interface with a compatible model implementation.

For how to run a particular demo/model pair, refer to the format listed here: Running a model.

items.title: Interactive Experiences
items.text: HandDreamsMove generated robot hands with virtual or physical controllers. Crazy RobotaxiDrive, collect passengers, or race with keyboard, gamepad, or wheel controls. Interactive DriveRun a world-model-driven driving session.

items.title: Model Interfaces
items.text: Action2VControl generation with direct actions such as keyboard and mouse input. Cam2VControl a camera through a generated world interactively. T2VGenerate video from text and submit prompts without unloading the model. V2VRestore or upscale a local or remote video source. Minimal T2VTutorial application with an ImGui prompt field and a per-prompt model cache.

items.title: Action2V
items.text:
Action2V is an interactive FlashDreams v2 application for world models driven by direct keyboard and mouse actions. A selected model supplies its pipeline, first-frame resolution, and action-vocabulary mapping.

Four-second Action2V demo preview generated by FlashDreams.

items.title: Quick Start:
items.text: Waypoint 1.5

items.title: Controls
items.text:
Action2V preserves held keyboard and mouse-button state. Pointer motion and wheel deltas are consumed once per model action. Reset and focus loss clear held state and pointer history.

The selected model maps those model-neutral inputs to its own action vocabulary. Use --reset-key to choose the ASCII letter that resets the current session.

items.title: Demo Arguments
items.text: Argument Description --image-path PATH Use an RGB or RGBA image to establish the initial world state. --example-data, --no-example-data Enable or disable the selected model's example image. --device DEVICE Select the model device. --total-blocks N Stop after this many generated action blocks. --ui, --no-ui Enable or disable interactive pointer capture. --seed N Override the model RNG seed for reproducible generation. --mouse-sensitivity SCALE Multiply pointer motion by a finite, non-negative scale. Default: 1.0. --reset-key CHAR Reset the current session when this ASCII letter is pressed. Default: T.

items.title: Model-free demo
items.text:
Use the packaged example image to exercise Action2V without loading a model:

uv run --package flashdreams-action2v flashdreams-run-v2 action2v-dummy \
  --mode webrtc -- --example-data

items.title: Tests
items.text: uv run --no-sync pytest apps/action2v/tests -m ci_cpu

items.title: Cam2V
items.text:
Cam2V is an interactive FlashDreams v2 camera-to-video application. It turns keyboard camera controls, a prompt, and model-specific starting inputs into a long-running generated view.

Four-second Cam2V demo preview generated by FlashDreams.

items.title: Quick Start:
items.text: LingBot-World SANA-WM

items.title: Controls
items.text:
Keys Action W / S, Up / Down Move forward / backward. A / D, J / L Yaw left / right. Q / E Strafe left / right. I / K Pitch up / down.

Losing browser focus clears held keys. Presentation pacing includes optional post-processing; model-only timing remains separate.

items.title: Demo Arguments
items.text: Argument Description --prompt TEXT, --prompt-path PATH Set the text prompt directly or from a file. --image-path PATH Set the first frame. --pose-path PATH Set a pose trace used by the model adapter. --intrinsic-path PATH Set camera calibration. --world-scale FLOAT Set the camera-motion scale. --example-data, --no-example-data Enable or disable packaged/example inputs. --example-idx INT Select an example input. --device DEVICE Select the model device. --total-blocks INT Stop after this many autoregressive chunks. --warmup-blocks INT Set chunks excluded from steady-state FPS. --ui, --no-ui Enable or disable the controls/status overlay. --compile, --no-compile Enable or disable model compilation. --postprocess-preset NAME Select an installed generated-video post-processing preset. --postprocess-chunk-size {8,16} Set the steady post-processing window. Default: 8. --postprocess-compile, --no-postprocess-compile Enable or disable postprocessor compilation. --postprocess-comparison-ui, --no-postprocess-comparison-ui Show synchronized original and post-processed panes. --seed INT Override the diffusion seed.

items.title: Post-processing comparison
items.text:
With a postprocessor configured, --postprocess-comparison-ui shows the original video on the left and the post-processed video on the right:

uv run --no-sync flashdreams-run-v2 DEMO_MODEL_SLUG \
  --mode webrtc --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8089 -- \
  --postprocess-preset PRESET --postprocess-comparison-ui

The mode requires the UI and a frame-preserving postprocessor. It doubles the delivered video width and may increase encoding and transfer cost.

items.title: Model-free demo
items.text:
Exercise the Cam2V UI without loading a model:

uv run --no-sync flashdreams-run-v2 cam2v-dummy --mode webrtc \
  --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8089 -- \
  --step-wait-seconds 0.9 --frames-per-chunk 12

items.title: Tests
items.text: uv run --no-sync pytest apps/cam2v/tests -m ci_cpu

items.title: Crazy Robotaxi
items.text:
Drive a taxi, collect fares, race, or explore with a keyboard, gamepad, or steering wheel. The game engine handles motion, collisions, and scoring.

OmniDreams generates the street view from the simulated HD map (RGB image of color-coded boxes and lines).

HUD and navigation markers come from the game engine.

Four-second Crazy Robotaxi demo preview generated by FlashDreams.

items.title: Quick Start:
items.text:
OmniDreams

The model guide covers installation, GPU preset selection, and browser or native-window startup.

items.title: Start playing
items.text:
1. Select Taxi (pick up and drop off passengers before time expires), Race (timed checkpoints), or Free Roam (explore without objectives).
  2. Choose Boulevard District for suburban streets and traffic, or FlashDreams Raceway for a curved four-lane course.
  3. Drive with WASD and brake with Space. Press Escape for menus.

Visuals of this game are expected to drift from the HDMap over-time.

For optional dynamic-prompts/weather, refer to Optional live-edit abilities section.

items.title: Controls
items.text:
Open CONTROLS from the mode menu, then choose KEYBOARD, GAMEPAD, or WHEEL. Each gameplay action has primary and secondary binding slots. Select a slot and press the desired key or device control. Escape is a valid keyboard binding. Backspace, Delete, or CLEAR unbinds the slot, while CANCEL stops capture without changing it. Reusing an existing binding swaps it with the previous slot. SAVE writes the current device without leaving its page, and RESET TO DEFAULTS affects only that device.

Bindings are stored as three independent sparse YAML documents under $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/crazy-robotaxi/controls/, or ~/.config/crazy-robotaxi/controls/ when XDG_CONFIG_HOME is unset: keyboard.yaml, gamepad.yaml, and wheel.yaml. Use the CLI-only --controls-dir PATH option to select another directory. Control changes take effect after restarting the current application process.

items.title: Keyboard
items.text:
Control Action W or Up Arrow Drive forward S or Down Arrow Brake, then reverse after stopping A or Left Arrow Steer left D or Right Arrow Steer right Space Apply the handbrake and cancel throttle R Restart the current game H Hide or show the HUD control tooltips M Toggle the model's HD-map conditioning view Escape Return to the previous menu, then exit from the mode screen; also the default gameplay return-to-menu binding Enter Submit the focused leaderboard name (fixed)

Menu choices and leaderboard buttons can also be clicked with the mouse.

items.title: Controller
items.text:
The Gamepad Controls screen uses one button-label convention at a time. Set game.gamepad_button_style to Xbox, PlayStation, or Nintendo Switch in the Options screen or user-authored settings YAML. Xbox labels are the default.

Control Action Left stick Steer Right trigger (RT by default) Throttle Left trigger (LT by default) Brake, then reverse after stopping Menu button Restart the current game Steering wheel and pedals Use normalized steering, throttle, and brake input

A connected gamepad or wheel takes precedence over keyboard driving input. Menu navigation remains mouse and keyboard controlled. Gamepad and wheel handbrake, control-hint, HD-map, and live-edit actions are supported. The gamepad supplies default bindings for them; the wheel leaves them unbound by default. Wheel bindings use the semantic steering, throttle, brake, clutch, and button values supplied by the runtime; physical device calibration remains a runtime concern.

items.title: Demo Arguments
items.text:
Argument Description --config PATH Load user settings from a specific YAML file. --controls-dir PATH Load keyboard, gamepad, and wheel bindings from a specific directory. --map PATH Load an authored .robotaxi.yaml map. --width N, --height N Set generated-frame dimensions. --display-width N, --display-height N Set presentation dimensions independently of generation. --force-map-recompile Recompile the selected map before launch. --ui, --no-ui Enable or disable the HUD. Headless runs require --game-mode, --map, and --total-blocks. --device DEVICE Select the application device. --total-blocks N Stop after this many generated blocks. --game-time-s SECONDS Override the taxi-mode time limit. --seed N Set both gameplay and model seeds. --game-seed N, --model-seed N Set gameplay and model seeds independently. --high-scores PATH Store taxi-mode high scores at a specific path. --game-mode {taxi,race,free-roam} Start directly in taxi, race, or Free-Roam mode. --visual-flare, --no-visual-flare Enable or disable visual flare. --race-course NAME Select a race course from the active map. --race-times PATH Store race times at a specific path. --compile, --no-compile Enable or disable model compilation. --profile-pipeline Log model-loop timing and real-time budget diagnostics. --prewarm-blocks N Generate hidden neutral blocks before presentation. Default: 8; 0 disables prewarming. --profile-input-latency [PATH] Show input diagnostics and write a chunk-lifecycle trace. --show-fps, --no-show-fps Show or hide generated-video FPS in the HUD.

Live-edit flags are described in Optional live-edit abilities.

items.title: Options and user configuration
items.text:
The mode menu has CONTROLS and OPTIONS buttons. The Options screen is generated from the same typed settings tree used at startup, with pages for game, model, renderer, presentation, live edit, runtime, and diagnostics. SAVE atomically updates the user YAML without leaving the screen. EXIT returns to the mode menu and changes to EXIT WITHOUT SAVING while the draft is dirty. RESET TO DEFAULTS resets the draft. HUD and presentation settings apply when saved. Other startup settings display RESTART REQUIRED FOR SETTINGS TO TAKE EFFECT because they need a new process.

By default, settings are loaded from $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/crazy-robotaxi/config.yaml, or ~/.config/crazy-robotaxi/config.yaml when XDG_CONFIG_HOME is unset. The file is created only after the first save. Use --config PATH to select another user-authored file. YAML values are sparse overrides on the selected runner's defaults, and retained comments survive Options saves. Explicit application CLI arguments override YAML for the current run without rewriting the saved value; the Options screen labels affected fields.

For example:

schema_version: 1
game:
  gamepad_button_style: PlayStation
  taxi:
    seed: 1234
    rules:
      global_time_s: 90.0
model:
  pipeline:
    diffusion_model:
      seed: 5678
presentation:
  width: 1920
  height: 1080
  show_fps: true
live_edit:
  weather:
    enabled: true

Mode, map, and race-course selections are intentionally CLI-only and do not appear in the YAML or Options screen. Passing --game-mode, --map, and --race-course skips their corresponding startup menus; omitted selections remain in the normal menu flow. Model diffusion and gameplay seeds are independent. Selecting mystery items automatically enables style editing, while rain or snow items automatically enable weather editing.

items.title: Race mode
items.text:
Bundled maps can define ordered race courses. Start with the included raceway and select the grand-prix course in the menu:

uv run flashdreams-run-v2 DEMO_MODEL_SLUG --mode native-window -- \
  --map apps/crazy_robotaxi/crazy_robotaxi/maps/flashdreams_raceway.robotaxi.yaml \
  --game-mode race

Race times are stored per map and course. Use --race-times PATH to choose a different leaderboard file.

items.title: Free-Roam mode
items.text: Choose FREE-ROAM from the mode menu, then choose a map. Free-Roam keeps driving and enabled live-edit abilities available without fares, checkpoints, a timer, or a score. No race-course selection is needed.

items.title: Optional live-edit abilities
items.text:
Live-edit features are disabled by default due to performance overhead.

Enable them via one of the following:

  • Game menu:

    1. open OPTIONS → LIVE EDIT

    2. enable the feature

    3. SAVE

    4. restart the application.

  • Command-line arguments:

uv run flashdreams-run-v2 DEMO_MODEL_SLUG --mode native-window -- \
  --live-edit-coins \
  --live-edit-items \
  --live-edit-weather \
  --live-edit-style \
  --live-edit-obstacle \
  --live-edit-dynamic-prompts

items.title: Live-edit abilities
items.text:
When enabled:

  • C toggles coins
  • K cycles style skins
  • V cycles weather
  • O spawns a crossing obstacle

Actions will appear as buttons in the HUD. Weather cannot change while a style is active (i.e. non-default style). When enabled, style mode downloads missing model assets during application startup and caches them under artifacts/crazy_robotaxi/live_edit. Explicit checkpoint paths skip the corresponding downloads.

Dynamic prompts append selected descriptions of the current road, upcoming map node and curve, and taxi motion to the active prompt. Choose which fragments to include in LIVE EDIT → Dynamic Prompts in Options. Complete combined prompts are encoded and retained lazily, so the first visit to a new combination may pause briefly and sessions with many unique combinations retain more GPU memory.

Style, weather, active dynamic prompts, and guided obstacles need the Python transformer hooks. When one of those features is enabled, the application automatically disables native DiT acceleration and logs the reason. Native VAE acceleration and the remaining performance configuration stay enabled; pixel-only features such as coins, items, and unguided obstacles keep native DiT acceleration.

items.title: Authored maps
items.text:
Maps are strict semantic .robotaxi.yaml documents. Validate or preview them without loading a model:

uv run --package crazy-robotaxi crazy-robotaxi-map validate path/to/city.robotaxi.yaml
uv run --package crazy-robotaxi crazy-robotaxi-map compile path/to/city.robotaxi.yaml
uv run --package crazy-robotaxi crazy-robotaxi-map preview \
  path/to/city.robotaxi.yaml --output city.svg
uv run --package crazy-robotaxi crazy-robotaxi-map preview-spawn \
  path/to/city.robotaxi.yaml --spawn taxi_start --output taxi_start.png

Each spawn can define both a full prompt for normal play and a shorter prompt_context base for active dynamic prompts. Selected fragments are appended to that base, falling back to prompt when prompt_context is absent.

items.title: HandDreams
items.text:
Control generated robot hands with virtual or physical controllers. No physical robot is controlled.

HandDreams with a custom scene catalog. Recording from the HandDreams guide PR.

items.title: Quick Start
items.text: Cosmos3 Nano Sim Bimanual

items.title: Controls
items.text:
After connecting virtual controllers or physical controllers, click a scene thumbnail or use arrow keys → Enter. With virtual controllers, hold either Trig until the progress bar fills, then release both triggers to begin. With physical controllers, complete calibration. Scene changes repeat calibration.

Input Action Controller position/rotation Move the corresponding hand. Trig / Index Trigger Squeeze to close the gripper; release to open. Escape Return to scene selection and start a fresh rollout.

XR CONTROL shows controller input; the generated pose can differ. The GA checkpoint can sometimes open or close grippers without matching input.

items.title: Demo Arguments
items.text: Argument Default Purpose --accept-eula and --isaac-teleop-accept-eula Unset Specify that you have already accepted the 'Isaac Teleop/CloudXR eula' terms. Accept via the canonical launch.py setup-isaac-teleop command. --position-gain 1.2 Scale controller translation. --control-fps Scene FPS Set controller sampling and model temporal conditioning, independently of UI refresh. --sample-dir PATH Downloaded scenes Use a server folder with up to five scene subdirectories, each containing first_frame.jpg and scene.json. --scene-path PATH Unset Load one scene folder (containing first_frame.jpg and scene.json) at startup.

items.title: Setup Isaac Teleop
items.text:
Run from flashdreams root:

uv run --no-project --python 3.12 python \
  integrations_v2/cosmos3_nano_sim_bimanual/apps/handdreams/launch.py setup-isaac-teleop

Review the displayed Isaac Teleop/CloudXR terms and type yes if you accept. You may only use --accept-eula and --isaac-teleop-accept-eula for this demo if you have already accepted the 'Isaac Teleop/CloudXR eula' terms.

items.title: Connect Virtual Controllers
items.text:
Ensure you have completed Isaac Teleop setup on your server that will run the HandDreams demo.

  1. Open http://<server-address>:8081/ and wait for scene selection.
  2. Click Isaac Teleop Web Client: Open Link. Keep both tabs open.
  3. Verify the certificate link points to your server's https://<server-address>:48322/, accept its development certificate, and return to Teleop.
  4. Keep the default settings and click CONNECT. Both controller panels should appear, and the viewer should report both tracked.
  5. Select a scene, hold either Trig until the progress bar fills, then release both triggers. Move a controller to move its generated hand.

Use a trusted network where viewer TCP 8081, Teleop HTTPS 48322, and WebRTC media traffic can reach the server. Stop with Ctrl+C.

items.title: Initial Setup
items.text:
Ensure you have completed Isaac Teleop setup on your server that will run the HandDreams demo. Ensure that if you plan to use a laptop-connected Quest, you must also complete the setup there as well.

Run all future launch commands from the flashdreams repository root.

First, connect a Quest headset by USB to your server or a Ubuntu laptop. On the connected machine, install ADB and coturn:

sudo apt install adb coturn
adb devices

Enable Quest Developer Mode and approve USB debugging in the headset. Run adb devices again and confirm the headset shows as device, not unauthorized. Keep Quest Wi-Fi connected with an IPv4 address; an offline access point works. Controller data travels over USB; watch generated video in the demo viewer.

Move on to Headset Connected to the Server or Headset Connected to a Laptop depending on where the headset is connected.

items.title: Headset Connected to the Server
items.text:
Connect and authorize the Quest before launching anything on the server.

For a native window view of the hands-demo, run from the server's graphical desktop:

env -u QUEST_META_PIN uv run --no-sync flashdreams-run-v2 handdreams \
  --mode native-window \
  --isaac-teleop-accept-eula \
  --quest-accept-server-certificate

# Add `--quest-device <SERIAL>` if needed to select a specific headset.
# `env -u QUEST_META_PIN` removes legacy PIN setting for the life-time of `flashdreams-run-v2`.
# `--quest-accept-server-certificate` allows quest to accept a CloudXR development certificate. Relay TLS verification stays enabled.

For WebRTC output use the following command:

SERVER_IP=127.0.0.1  # Use the server's reachable LAN IPv4 for a remote browser
env -u QUEST_META_PIN uv run --no-sync flashdreams-run-v2 handdreams \
  --mode webrtc --host "$SERVER_IP" --port 8081 \
  --controller-host "$SERVER_IP" \
  --isaac-teleop-accept-eula \
  --quest-accept-server-certificate

# Use the server's LAN IPv4 for `SERVER_IP`.
# Connect to `http://<SERVER_IP>:8081/`.
# The headset browser connects automatically; do not connect a virtual client.

Continue with calibration.

items.title: Headset Connected to a Laptop
items.text:
For native output on the server, change its mode to native-window but retain --controller-host "<SERVER_IP>"; the laptop command is unchanged.

With a SERVER_IP and PORT pair that is reachable by your laptop, on the server, run either: 1. [For Browser View On Laptop/Server Of Demo] The WebRTC command in the Headset Connected to the Server section above 2. [For Native Window View On Server Of Demo] The native window command in the Headset Connected to the Server section above. Add --controller-host "$SERVER_IP" to the native-window command.

With ssh/scp, a verified server host key, and key/agent login, check that this succeeds without a password prompt:

ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=yes -o BatchMode=yes "<USER>@<SERVER_IP>" true

On your laptop, start the laptop client:

env -u QUEST_META_PIN uv run --no-project --python 3.12 python \
  integrations_v2/cosmos3_nano_sim_bimanual/apps/handdreams/launch.py remote-vr \
  --server "<USER>@<SERVER_IP>" \
  --accept-eula \
  --accept-server-certificate

# `--accept-server-certificate` allows the laptop to accept a CloudXR development certificate from the server.

This command will prepare controller dependencies, copy credentials, and copy web assets over SSH to your laptop; model weights remain on the server. Your laptop needs direct access to server TCP 8445 since SSH is not setup to tunnel its connection.

You may now open http://<SERVER_IP>:8081/ in your browser.

Continue with calibration.

items.title: Physical-Controller Calibration
items.text:
1. Press the headset's power button when prompted to wake it. Clear any passcode or privacy screen and approve immersive-VR and local-network permissions if requested.
  2. In the demo viewer, click a scene thumbnail or use arrow keys → Enter.
  3. Hold the controllers side by side at the same height. Squeeze both index triggers fully for 1 second, until gray guides appear.
  4. Release both triggers and match the guides with both claws open. Hold the aligned pose for 1 second to start generation, then move the controllers to control the hands.

Press keyboard B in the viewer to retry a server-attached Quest, then wake the headset when prompted. For a laptop Quest, stop and restart remote-vr. Stop both the server and laptop client with Ctrl+C; cleanup puts the managed headset to sleep. Closing only the viewer tab leaves the server running.

You should now be able to control the hands with the physical controllers.

items.title: Scene Data
items.text: The demo downloads Fold the T-shirt, Fold the shorts, and Open the tissue box from AgiBotWorld-Beta using your Hugging Face credentials. Scene data is not bundled with the demo.

items.title: Troubleshooting
items.text:
• Virtual controller keeps sliding: in the Teleop toolbar, click the game-controller icon to switch to hands, then the hand icon to switch back. Confirm both controllers are tracked and reselect the scene if needed.
  • No connection: check the server address, development certificate, browser local-network permission, and WebRTC/firewall connectivity.
  • Gripper drift or degrading video: press Escape and select the scene again for a fresh rollout.

items.title: Interactive Drive
items.text:
Interactive Drive is a long-running FlashDreams v2 driving application with scene and variant selection, driving telemetry, post-processing controls, and a (only omnidreams) BEV minimap.

Four-second Interactive Drive demo preview generated by FlashDreams.

items.title: Quick Start:
items.text: OmniDreams Cosmos3 Nano Sim Auto

items.title: Keyboard
items.text: Key Action W or Up arrow Accelerate forward. S or Down arrow Accelerate in reverse. A or Left arrow Steer left. D or Right arrow Steer right. R Restart the current scene. Space Brake; while held, throttle is suppressed. 1 Show the RGB view. 2 Show the HD-map conditioning view. 3 Show the PhysX collider view.

items.title: Controller
items.text:
Standard-mapped gamepads use these controls:

Control Action Left stick, push forward+tilt Steer. Right trigger Accelerate in the selected gear. Left trigger Brake. R (hold) Select reverse gear; releasing returns to Drive. Start / + (Plus) Restart the current rollout.

View selection does not currently have controller bindings. No other gamepad sticks, axes, or buttons are used. A connected steering wheel uses its steering, throttle, and brake inputs directly.

items.title: Steering wheel setup
items.text:
Calibrate a wheel and pedals with:

uv run --package flashdreams-interactive-drive-v2 interactive-drive-configuration

Interactive Drive loads the default profile on later launches. One profile can bind a wheel and separately connected pedals. Force feedback requires write access to /dev/input/* and the appropriate Linux driver:

Vendor Driver Thrustmaster hid-tmff2, plus hid-tminit or tmdrv for wheel-mode initialization Fanatec hid-fanatecff, with the base in PC mode Logitech In-kernel hid-lg4ff, new-lg4ff, or the HID++ driver for the G920 and Xbox/PC G923

items.title: Demo Arguments
items.text:
Unsupported is a section to note partially/fully non-functional commands for a given model.

Argument Description Unsupported --scene PATH Choose a local scene file: OmniDreams uses a USDZ scene; Cosmos3 Nano Sim Auto uses a Scene bundle. — --prompt TEXT Override the prompt stored in the selected scene variant. — --camera NAME Select a camera from the scene. Default: camera_front_wide_120fov. Cosmos3 Nano Sim Auto accepts an ordered comma-separated subset, do not mix with --views. — --variant NAME Select the scene's initial-frame and prompt variant. Default: default. cosmos3-nano-sim-auto --total-blocks N Stop after this many generated blocks; 0 runs until the session is stopped. Default: 0. — --fps N Set the application frame rate. Default: 30. — --width N Set the output width. The selected demo-model slug supplies the default. — --height N Set the output height. The selected demo-model slug supplies the default. — --view {rgb,hdmap,physx} Select the initial RGB, HD-map conditioning, or PhysX collider view. Default: rgb. cosmos3-nano-sim-auto (physx) --no-ui Present model output directly without creating the HUD or rendering its BEV minimap. — --game-mode Enable the speed limit. cosmos3-nano-sim-auto (missing collision) --postprocess-preset NAME Start with a registered video post-processing preset enabled. Default: none. — --postprocess-device DEVICE Select the postprocessor device independently. Default: cuda:0. — --world-model-device DEVICE Select the model device. Default: cuda:0. — --raster-device DEVICE Select the Ludus raster device independently. Default: cuda:0. cosmos3-nano-sim-auto --world-model-seed N Pin the seed used for each rollout. — --world-model-debug-condition-frame-dir PATH Override first-chunk condition frames for debugging. cosmos3-nano-sim-auto --views N Select the number of cameras to display. Allowed: 1, 4 or 7. Do not mix with --camera omnidreams --lidar Show the LiDAR point cloud. Default: False. Cosmos3 Nano Sim Auto accepts this option. omnidreams

For OmniDreams, use the default scene, select its rain variant, override its prompt, and enable RTX super resolution:

uv run flashdreams-run-v2 interactive-drive-omnidreams --mode webrtc -- \
    --variant rain --prompt "A rainy night drive" \
    --game-mode --postprocess-preset rtx-super-resolution

For Cosmos3 Nano Sim Auto, use the rain scene, override its prompt, and enable RTX super resolution:

uv run flashdreams-run-v2 interactive-drive-cosmos3-nano-sim-auto --mode webrtc -- \
    --scene clipgt-residential-rain-iter1500 --prompt "A rainy night drive" \
    --game-mode --postprocess-preset rtx-super-resolution

Render a video of the demo without ui or dropped frames: 

uv run flashdreams-run-v2 DEMO_MODEL_SLUG \
    --mode mp4 --output-path artifacts/test/interactive-drive.mp4 \
    --timeout unbound \
    --backpressure-mode block --presentation-mode on_demand -- \
    --no-ui --total-blocks 60

The HUD's view button cycles through RGB → HDMAP → PHYSX for omnidreams and RGB → HDMAP for cosmos3-nano-sim-auto.

When --postprocess-preset is set, the preset starts enabled and the HUD's Post-processing checkbox can toggle it between generated chunks. Without a preset, the checkbox is hidden. Run uv run --no-sync flashdreams-run-v2 DEMO_MODEL_SLUG -- --help to list registered post-processing presets. The built-in rtx-* presets require the optional NVIDIA VFX dependency, installable with uv pip install 'flashdreams[rtx-postprocess]', and supported RTX hardware.

items.title: Minimal T2V
items.text: Minimal T2V is the tutorial application built in Create a demo. It owns an ImGui prompt field, a model loop, and a per-prompt generation cache.

items.title: Quick Start:
items.text: Wan 2.1

items.title: Demo Arguments
items.text:
Edit the prompt and click Send to start a new clip. Empty text pauses generation. The window remains open between clips; close it to stop.

App argument Default Purpose --default-prompt Empty Initial prompt; omit it to wait for input. --device cuda Device on which to load the model.

items.title: T2V
items.text:
T2V is a FlashDreams v2 text-to-video application. It accepts an initial text prompt, keeps the selected model resident, and can start fresh generation sessions from an interactive prompt field.

Four-second T2V demo preview generated by FlashDreams.

items.title: Quick Start:
items.text: Self-Forcing Causal-Forcing Causal Wan 2.2 Wan 2.1 Wan 2.2 Cosmos-Predict2.5

items.title: Controls
items.text: An interactive WebRTC run shows a prompt field over the latest generated frame. Submitting it starts a fresh session and rollout cache without unloading the model. Reaching --total-blocks leaves the final frame and prompt UI active. Model adapters may add startup inputs such as a first-frame image.

items.title: Demo Arguments
items.text:
Argument Description --prompt TEXT Set the optional initial prompt; explicitly empty text is rejected. --total-blocks N Set the number of autoregressive blocks; the selected model supplies the default. --device DEVICE Select the model device. Default: cuda. --compile, --no-compile Override model compilation. --seed N Override the diffusion seed for reproducible generation. --ui, --no-ui Enable or disable the interactive prompt overlay.

Bidirectional models generate a complete clip in one block and require --total-blocks 1. Image-conditioned implementations may additionally require --image-path.

For example, write a generated clip to MP4:

uv run flashdreams-run-v2 DEMO_MODEL_SLUG \
  --output-path clip.mp4 --timeout unbound -- \
  --prompt "A cat surfing"

To keep the model resident and submit prompts from a browser:

uv run flashdreams-run-v2 DEMO_MODEL_SLUG \
  --mode webrtc --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8089

items.title: Tests
items.text: uv run --no-sync pytest apps/t2v/tests -m ci_cpu

items.title: V2V
items.text:
V2V is a finite FlashDreams v2 video-to-video application. It restores or upscales a selected local or remote video and writes or streams the result.

Four-second V2V demo preview generated by FlashDreams.

items.title: Quick Start:
items.text: FlashVSR SwiftVR

items.title: Controls
items.text: None. V2V is uninteractive and stops after the configured source-video chunks have been processed.

items.title: Demo Arguments
items.text:
Argument Description --video-path PATH_OR_URL Select a local video or HTTP(S) URL. Omit it to use the bounded Big Buck Bunny default. --max-chunks N Limit the number of source-video chunks to process.

For example, process a local input and write the result to MP4:

uv run flashdreams-run-v2 DEMO_MODEL_SLUG \
  --output-path restored.mp4 --timeout unbound -- --video-path input.mp4

Use --mode webrtc or --mode native-window instead of --output-path to watch the run live.

items.text:
Choose a section to browse the command-line, application, inference, and project tooling documentation.

CLI ReferenceLaunch demos and configure FlashDreams from the command line. Demo APIBuild, configure, launch, and package user-facing applications. Inferencing APIImplement models, components, and streaming inference pipelines. ToolingBuild the website and package FlashDreams programs for offline use. items.title: Command Shape To Run A Demo/Model
items.text:
This section will only cover <System Arguments>. Refer to the Running a model section for more information on <Demo Preset> and <Demo Arguments>: 

uv run flashdreams-run-v2 <Demo Preset> <System Arguments> -- <Demo Arguments>

items.title: General
items.text: Argument Description --timeout {SECONDS,unbound} Bound the whole application run, including initialization and replacement sessions. --total-model-steps {N,unbound} Bound model steps across the whole application run, including replacement sessions. --mode {mp4,webrtc,native-window} Select file, browser, or local-window presentation. Default: mp4. --stats-path PATH Write JSON model-step measurements and enable synchronized per-stage pipeline profiling.

items.title: MP4 Specific
items.text: Argument Description --output-path PATH MP4 destination. Required in MP4 mode.

items.title: WebRTC Specific
items.text: Argument Description --host HOST Interface to serve on. Default: 127.0.0.1; use 0.0.0.0 for remote clients. --port PORT Port to serve on. Default: 0, which selects an available port.

items.title: Native Window Specific
items.text: Argument Description --window-title TITLE Native window title. Default: FlashDreams.

items.title: Default Demo Session Overrides
items.text:
These options override the default demo session values requested by a particular demo implementation. Omit them to use the application's default values.

Argument Description --pixel-width N Override generated-frame width. --pixel-height N Override generated-frame height. --fps N Override the generated-frame playback rate. --layout {tchw,btchw,bcthw,bvtchw} Override generated tensor layout. --backpressure-mode {block,drop_oldest} Choose full-queue behavior: block waits for capacity to retain generated chunks; drop_oldest discards the oldest queued chunk to favor recent output. --presentation-mode {on_demand,continuous} Choose rendering behavior: on_demand presents each selected model frame when it arrives; continuous keeps the UI responsive between model frames by reusing the newest frame.

items.title: Examples
items.text:
Stream to a browser:

uv run flashdreams-run-v2 DEMO_MODEL_SLUG --mode webrtc --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8089

Write every generated frame in order to an MP4:

uv run flashdreams-run-v2 DEMO_MODEL_SLUG --mode mp4 --output-path output.mp4 \
  --timeout unbound --backpressure-mode block --presentation-mode on_demand

MP4 mode requires --timeout and/or --total-model-steps; pass unbound to name an explicit unlimited policy. WebRTC and native-window modes may omit both limits. When a session is replaced, it receives the time and model steps left for the whole run.

Preload and validate a v2 application without opening a window:

uv run --no-sync flashdreams-run-v2 cam2v-lingbot \
  --preload-application -- --example-data

Preload runs IApplication.init and one model block. It defaults to warning; set FLASHDREAMS_PREPARATION_POLICY to none, warn, or error. Findings are written to preparation_issues.txt in the FlashDreams cache, or to FLASHDREAMS_PREPARATION_ISSUES_PATH when set. Use --skip-preload-validation to skip the first-block validation.

Open a local native window:

uv run flashdreams-run-v2 DEMO_MODEL_SLUG --mode native-window --window-title FlashDreams

One application, for as long as the process runs.

Parses its own arguments and holds whatever its sessions share, such as a checkpoint or a compiled pipeline. It outlives every session it creates, so that shared state is loaded once here and released in :meth:close.

An application module implements this and :class:ISession. The runtime creates everything else and passes it in.

register_ui_loop(loop_type: type[IUILoop[Any]], *, state: Any = None, **kwargs: Any) -> IUILoop[Any]

Create and register the UI loop, and return it.

Omit this call to use the default UI. The loop is paced at the session's frames_per_second_for_ui.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default loop_type type[IUILoop[Any]]

UI loop class to instantiate.

required state Any

State the loop owns. Unlike a model loop, a UI loop is allowed to hold none.

None **kwargs Any

Passed to loop_type.

{}

Raises:

Type Description RuntimeError

The runtime already took the loops, or a UI loop was registered already.

TypeError

loop_type does not derive from :class:IUILoop.

Source code in flashdreams/flashdreams/api_v2/session.py 
@final
def register_ui_loop(
    self,
    loop_type: type[IUILoop[Any]],
    *,
    state: Any = None,
    **kwargs: Any,
) -> IUILoop[Any]:
    """Create and register the UI loop, and return it.

    Omit this call to use the default UI. The loop is paced at the session's
    ``frames_per_second_for_ui``.

    Args:
        loop_type: UI loop class to instantiate.
        state: State the loop owns. Unlike a model loop, a UI loop is
            allowed to hold none.
        **kwargs: Passed to ``loop_type``.

    Raises:
        RuntimeError: The runtime already took the loops, or a UI loop was
            registered already.
        TypeError: ``loop_type`` does not derive from :class:`IUILoop`.
    """
    if self._registrations_frozen:
        raise RuntimeError("Loop registrations are already in use.")
    if self._registered_ui_loop is not None:
        raise RuntimeError("The session already registered a UI loop.")
    if not issubclass(loop_type, IUILoop):
        raise TypeError("The UI loop must derive from IUILoop.")
    loop = loop_type(**kwargs)
    loop.register_session_loop_objects(
        state=state,
        frequency=self.session_desc.frames_per_second_for_ui,
        shutdown_event=self._shutdown_event,
        failure_queue=self._failure_queue,
        profiler=self._profiler,
    )
    loop.register_session_ui_loop_objects(
        session_desc=self.session_desc,
        presentation_manager=self._presentation_manager,
    )
    self._registered_ui_loop = loop
    return loop

@final
def register_model_loop(
    self,
    loop_type: type[IModelLoop[Any]],
    *,
    state: Any,
    **kwargs: Any,
) -> IModelLoop[Any]:
    """Create and register the model loop, and return it.

    The loop is paced at the session's ``frames_per_second_for_step``.

    Args:
        loop_type: Model loop class to instantiate.
        state: State the loop owns. Required, since a model loop with no
            state has nothing to generate from.
        **kwargs: Passed to ``loop_type``.

    Raises:
        RuntimeError: The runtime already took the loops, or a model loop
            was registered already.
        TypeError: ``loop_type`` does not derive from :class:`IModelLoop`.
    """
    if self._registrations_frozen:
        raise RuntimeError("Loop registrations are already in use.")
    if self._registered_model_loop is not None:
        raise RuntimeError("The session already registered a model loop.")
    if not issubclass(loop_type, IModelLoop):
        raise TypeError("The model loop must derive from IModelLoop.")
    loop = loop_type(**kwargs)
    loop.register_session_loop_objects(
        state=state,
        frequency=self.session_desc.frames_per_second_for_step,
        shutdown_event=self._shutdown_event,
        failure_queue=self._failure_queue,
        profiler=self._profiler,
    )
    self._registered_model_loop = loop
    return loop

items.title: flashdreams.api_v2.loop.IModelLoop
items.text:
Bases: ILoop[StateT], ABC

Loop that generates model results on the model thread.

:meth:ILoop.step must return list[StepResult] here, one entry per channel, with every channel reporting the same frame_count. An empty list means the step produced no presentable output.

Every admitted rank executes the same model step and ordered collectives. The integration owns TP/CP partitioning and must gather all CP shards needed for publication before the presenting rank returns non-empty results. Workers return [] only after all required collectives, including gathers. Gather before decoding when it needs the complete latent/view sequence; decoding may run only on the presenting rank when the model permits it. TP reductions that already replicate a complete value need no extra gather.

A run whose steps all present nothing still ends when the model loop does. Returning a bare :class:StepResult or None raises :class:TypeError.

@final
def step(self, step_index: int, events: UserInputEvents) -> list[StepResult]:
    """Render and composite one ImGui frame."""
    # User choses when to resize the UI, UI
    # must never resize the UI loop itself.
    # User may want to stretch the UI to fill
    # the overly-sized window.
    back_buffer: Tensor | None = None

    def draw(imgui: Any, index: int, current_events: UserInputEvents) -> None:
        nonlocal back_buffer
        back_buffer = self.step_ui(imgui, index, current_events)

    overlay = self.renderer.render(step_index, events, draw)
    back_buffer = prepare_ui_back_buffer(back_buffer, overlay)
    frame = self._presentation_manager.composite(back_buffer, overlay)
    return [
        StepResult(
            step_index=step_index,
            output=frame.unsqueeze(0),
            frame_count=1,
            output_layout=self.output_layout,
        )
    ]

items.title: Application
items.text:
IApplication holds resources shared by its sessions. Keep the constructor and session_desc() free of model loading: the runtime requests the description before init(). Here init() parses arguments and creates the pipeline; create_session() validates dimensions, layout, and frame rate before creating an uninitialized session. close() releases the shared pipeline reference.

The adapter supplies pipeline_config, a SessionDesc, and total_blocks, the maximum blocks per prompt. This app requires tchw output and a pipeline with initialize_cache, generate, and finalize methods.

# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright (c) 2026 NVIDIA CORPORATION & AFFILIATES. All rights reserved.
# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0

"""Minimal text-to-video application with lazy model initialization."""

import argparse
from collections.abc import Sequence
from typing import Any

from flashdreams.api_v2.application import IApplication
from flashdreams.runtime_v2.session_desc import SessionDesc
from flashdreams.runtime_v2.video_tensor import VideoTensorLayout

from .session import MinimalT2VSession


class MinimalT2VApplication(IApplication):
    """Tutorial app configured by a model adapter.

    The pipeline must accept text and latent dimensions in ``initialize_cache``
    and return ``tchw`` video from ``generate``, as Wan T2V pipelines do.
    """

    def __init__(
        self, pipeline_config: Any, desc: SessionDesc, total_blocks: int = 8
    ) -> None:
        """Keep model configuration without loading weights."""
        if desc.output_layout is not VideoTensorLayout.tchw:
            raise ValueError("Minimal T2V requires tchw output.")
        if total_blocks <= 0:
            raise ValueError("total_blocks must be positive.")
        self.pipeline_config = pipeline_config
        self.desc = desc
        self.total_blocks = total_blocks
        self.pipeline: Any = None
        self.prompt = ""

    def init(self, commandline_args: Sequence[str]) -> None:
        """Parse the initial prompt and load the shared pipeline."""
        parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Generate video from text.")
        parser.add_argument("--default-prompt", default="")
        parser.add_argument("--device", default="cuda")
        args = parser.parse_args(commandline_args)
        self.prompt = args.default_prompt.strip()
        self.pipeline = self.pipeline_config.setup().to(args.device).eval()

    def session_desc(self) -> SessionDesc:
        """Return the model adapter's output description."""
        return self.desc

    def create_session(self, session_desc: SessionDesc) -> MinimalT2VSession:
        """Create a session at the model's supported size and layout."""
        if self.pipeline is None:
            raise RuntimeError("Call init before create_session.")
        if (
            session_desc.video_width != self.desc.video_width
            or session_desc.video_height != self.desc.video_height
            or session_desc.output_layout != self.desc.output_layout
            or session_desc.frames_per_second_for_step
            != self.desc.frames_per_second_for_step
        ):
            raise ValueError("The session must match the model's output description.")
        ratio = self.pipeline.decoder.spatial_compression_ratio
        if session_desc.video_width % ratio or session_desc.video_height % ratio:
            raise ValueError(
                "Video dimensions must be divisible by decoder compression."
            )
        return MinimalT2VSession(
            self.pipeline, session_desc, self.prompt, self.total_blocks
        )

    def close(self) -> None:
        """Release the shared pipeline reference."""
        self.pipeline = None

items.title: Session
items.text:
ISession registers its model and UI loops during init(). Each loop owns its mutable state. The model loop runs inference; the UI loop handles input and presentation. Omit UI registration when the runtime's default frame display is sufficient.

# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright (c) 2026 NVIDIA CORPORATION & AFFILIATES. All rights reserved.
# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0

"""Session wiring for the Minimal T2V model and UI loops."""

from typing import Any

from flashdreams.api_v2.session import ISession
from flashdreams.runtime_v2.session_desc import SessionDesc

from .model_loop import TextToVideoLoop, TextToVideoState
from .ui_loop import MinimalT2VUILoop, MinimalT2VUIState


class MinimalT2VSession(ISession):
    """One interactive tutorial session sharing the application's pipeline."""

    def __init__(
        self, pipeline: Any, desc: SessionDesc, prompt: str, total_blocks: int
    ) -> None:
        """Keep session inputs until the runtime initializes the loops."""
        self.pipeline = pipeline
        self.desc = desc
        self.prompt = prompt
        self.total_blocks = total_blocks

    @property
    def session_desc(self) -> SessionDesc:
        """Return the description used to configure the window."""
        return self.desc

    def init(self) -> None:
        """Register independent model and UI state."""
        model_loop = self.register_model_loop(
            TextToVideoLoop,
            state=TextToVideoState(
                self.pipeline, self.desc, self.total_blocks, self.prompt
            ),
        )
        self.register_ui_loop(
            MinimalT2VUILoop,
            state=MinimalT2VUIState(model_loop, self.prompt),
            width=self.desc.video_width,
            height=self.desc.video_height,
        )

items.title: Model loop
items.text:
TextToVideoState keeps the prompt, cache, and per-prompt block index. TextToVideoLoop.step() initializes the cache lazily, generates and finalizes one block, and returns a StepResult with its frame count, layout, and metrics. Empty prompts or completed rollouts return [] while waiting for another prompt; the session remains open. reset() restarts the prompt, and close() releases its cache.

# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright (c) 2026 NVIDIA CORPORATION & AFFILIATES. All rights reserved.
# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0

"""Prompt and autoregressive cache owned by the tutorial model loop."""

from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Any

from flashdreams.api_v2.loop import IModelLoop
from flashdreams.runtime_v2.session_desc import SessionDesc
from flashdreams.runtime_v2.step_result import StepResult
from flashdreams.runtime_v2.user_input_events import UserInputEvents


@dataclass
class TextToVideoState:
    """Mutable rollout state, accessed on the model thread."""

    pipeline: Any
    """Text-conditioned pipeline shared across sessions."""
    desc: SessionDesc
    """Pixel dimensions and frame layout requested by the runtime."""
    total_blocks: int
    """Maximum blocks the selected model supports per prompt."""
    prompt: str = ""
    """Current prompt; empty text pauses generation."""
    cache: Any = None
    """Per-prompt cache, created lazily on the model thread."""
    index: int = 0
    """Next autoregressive block, independent of the runtime step index."""

    def set_prompt(self, prompt: str) -> None:
        """Start a fresh rollout or pause generation for empty text."""
        self.prompt = prompt.strip()
        self.cache = None
        self.index = 0


class TextToVideoLoop(IModelLoop[TextToVideoState]):
    """Generate bounded rollouts while waiting for further UI prompts."""

    def step(self, step_index: int, events: UserInputEvents) -> list[StepResult]:
        """Generate and finalize one block, or wait for another prompt."""
        state = self.state
        if not state.prompt or state.index >= state.total_blocks:
            return []
        if state.cache is None:
            ratio = state.pipeline.decoder.spatial_compression_ratio
            state.cache = state.pipeline.initialize_cache(
                text=[state.prompt],
                height=state.desc.video_height // ratio,
                width=state.desc.video_width // ratio,
            )
        frames = state.pipeline.generate(
            autoregressive_index=state.index, cache=state.cache
        )
        metrics = state.pipeline.finalize(
            autoregressive_index=state.index, cache=state.cache
        )
        state.index += 1
        return [
            StepResult(
                step_index=step_index,
                output=frames.detach(),
                frame_count=int(frames.shape[0]),
                output_layout=state.desc.output_layout,
                metrics=metrics,
            )
        ]

    def reset(self) -> None:
        """Restart the current prompt after a runtime reset."""
        self.state.set_prompt(self.state.prompt)

    def close(self) -> None:
        """Release the per-prompt cache."""
        self.state.cache = None

items.title: UI loop
items.text:
MinimalT2VUILoop.step_ui() draws the prompt field and Send button. invoke_async queues a prompt update on the model thread; capture the submitted text so later edits cannot change that queued message. The UI presents the latest model frame without directly modifying model state.

# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright (c) 2026 NVIDIA CORPORATION & AFFILIATES. All rights reserved.
# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0

"""ImGui prompt controls sending messages to the tutorial model loop."""

from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, Any

from torch import Tensor

from flashdreams.api_v2.loop import IModelLoop, invoke_async
from flashdreams.runtime_v2.imgui_ui_loop import ImGuiUILoop
from flashdreams.runtime_v2.user_input_events import UserInputEvents

if TYPE_CHECKING:
    from .model_loop import TextToVideoState


@dataclass
class MinimalT2VUIState:
    """Editable prompt owned by the UI thread."""

    model_loop: IModelLoop["TextToVideoState"]
    """Destination of prompt update messages."""
    text: str = ""
    """Text currently displayed in the prompt field."""


class MinimalT2VUILoop(ImGuiUILoop[MinimalT2VUIState]):
    """Send prompt updates without directly mutating model state."""

    def step_ui(
        self, imgui: Any, step_index: int, events: UserInputEvents
    ) -> Tensor | None:
        """Draw prompt controls over the latest generated frame."""
        imgui.begin("Minimal T2V")
        try:
            _, self.state.text = imgui.input_text("Prompt", self.state.text)
            if imgui.button("Send"):
                invoke_async(
                    self.state.model_loop,
                    lambda state, text=self.state.text: state.set_prompt(text),
                )
        finally:
            imgui.end()
        return self.presented_model_frame()

items.title: Check and document
items.text:
Run the existing CPU checks against a stub pipeline, without downloading weights:

uv run --no-sync pytest apps/minimal_t2v/tests -m ci_cpu

After adding an adapter, put install commands, requirements, and presets on its model page. Put controls and demo arguments on docs/source/demos/<demo>.md and link to the model's quick start. Add the demo to demos/.nav.yml and the matching category in demos/index.md. For a new model, also update models/.nav.yml, models/index.md, and the home gallery. Use Interactive serving to record a preview, then build the website.

items.title: Integrate model adapter for a demo
items.text:
An adapter is a package that contains the logic to connect a demo to a model.

In this example we connect the Minimal T2V application to Wan 2.1.
path: Integrate model adapter for a demo

items.title: Files to add or update
items.text:
After creating apps/minimal_t2v/, add the adapter package and update the website:

integrations_v2/wan21/
  config.py            # add a new pipeline config if desired
  apps/minimal_t2v/
    __init__.py       # add the package initializer
    adapter.py        # add the application factory
  pyproject.toml     # update dependencies, packages, and entry points

docs/source/
  models/
    wan21.md         # update: add Minimal T2V quick start, preset, and app-page link
    .nav.yml         # update when adding a new model page
    index.md         # add a card when adding a new model page
  demos/
    minimal_t2v.md   # update: link to the model's quick start

items.title: Create the adapter entry point
items.text:
Our adapter entry point is a factory function that creates an instance of our application based on the IApplication we defined.

This factory has the contract of:

def some_create_app() -> IApplication:
    ...

In our case we then make in integrations_v2/wan21/apps/minimal_t2v/adapter.py:

# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright (c) 2026 NVIDIA CORPORATION & AFFILIATES. All rights reserved.
# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0

"""Wan 2.1 adapter for the Minimal T2V application."""

from minimal_t2v import MinimalT2VApplication

from flashdreams.runtime_v2.session_desc import SessionDesc
from wan21.config import PIPELINE_WAN21_T2V_1PT3B_480P


def create_app() -> MinimalT2VApplication:
    """Return Minimal T2V with Wan 2.1's single-block pipeline."""
    return MinimalT2VApplication(
        pipeline_config=PIPELINE_WAN21_T2V_1PT3B_480P,
        desc=SessionDesc(
            video_width=832,
            video_height=480,
            frames_per_second_for_step=16,
        ),
        total_blocks=1,
    )

items.title: Register the application
items.text:
In integrations_v2/wan21/pyproject.toml:

  • Add flashdreams-minimal-t2v to project.dependencies and map it to { workspace = true } in tool.uv.sources.
  • Include wan21.apps.minimal_t2v in the setuptools packages.
  • Register minimal-t2v-wan21 under project.entry-points."flashdreams.applications_v2", pointing to wan21.apps.minimal_t2v.adapter:create_app.

The app must not depend on this integration. The existing package shows all three declarations:

uv run --no-sync flashdreams-run-v2 minimal-t2v-wan21 --mode native-window -- --default-prompt "A cat surfing"

Check argument parsing without constructing the model:

uv run --no-sync flashdreams-run-v2 minimal-t2v-wan21 -- --help

items.title: Adding a new pipeline configuration to pick from
items.text:
Modify integrations_v2/wan21/config.py to add a new pipeline config to wan21:

from flashdreams.infra.config import derive_config

PIPELINE_WAN21_T2V_SEED123 = derive_config(
    PIPELINE_WAN21_T2V_1PT3B_480P,
    name="wan21-t2v-1.3b-480p-seed123",
    diffusion_model={"seed": 123},
)

This defines a new pipeline config that is a copy of PIPELINE_WAN21_T2V_1PT3B_480P with the addition of a seed parameter to the diffusion model, setting the pipeline to always run diffusion with the same seed of 123.

To learn more about demo serving, see Interactive serving.

items.title: Interactive serving
items.text: Run a demo in a browser or a local window with flashdreams-run-v2. First install the integration using its model page.

items.title: Browser
items.text:
uv run --no-sync flashdreams-run-v2 APPLICATION_SLUG \
    --mode webrtc --host 127.0.0.1 --port 0

Open the URL printed by the server. Port 0 picks an available port. To accept connections from another machine, use --host 0.0.0.0 and a fixed port, then connect to the server's address.

items.title: Local window
items.text: uv run --no-sync flashdreams-run-v2 APPLICATION_SLUG --mode native-window

items.title: Demo arguments
items.text:
Runtime options go before --; demo options go after it:

uv run --no-sync flashdreams-run-v2 cam2v-lingbot \
    --mode webrtc --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8089 -- \
    --example-data --total-blocks 21

List runtime options with flashdreams-run-v2 --help. For this demo's options, use flashdreams-run-v2 cam2v-lingbot -- --help.

items.title: Input and display
items.text:
The runtime sends user input to the app's loops and displays their output. The app handles controls and model inputs. A custom UI loop can draw controls over the generated frames; otherwise, the runtime displays the frames directly.

Model and UI loops run on separate threads. Use invoke_async to send changes between them. Create a demo shows an ImGui text field sending a prompt to the model loop.

items.title: Record a preview
items.text:
Use an app that starts generating without menu or controller input. Supply its prompt, scene, or recorded actions explicitly; recording an idle UI produces no useful demonstration. For example, with the Wan 2.1 integration installed:

uv run --no-sync flashdreams-run-v2 t2v-wan21-t2v-1.3b-480p \
  --mode mp4 --output-path artifacts/t2v.mp4 \
  --total-model-steps 1 --timeout unbound \
  --backpressure-mode block --presentation-mode on_demand -- \
  --prompt "A cat surfing a wave" --no-ui

items.title: Multiple GPUs
items.text:
For a model adapter that supports distributed execution, launch all ranks:

uv run torchrun --nproc_per_node=2 --no-python flashdreams-run-v2 \
    cam2v-lingbot --mode webrtc -- --example-data --total-blocks 21

Rank zero handles the window and output. The session's parallel context synchronizes steps and inputs; the model integration handles parallel inference and gathers the output for rank zero.

See the CLI reference for runtime options, or Integrate model adapter for a demo to connect another model.

items.title: Profiling a demo
items.text: Nsight Systems shows the model thread, the UI thread and the GPU on one timeline, so you can see what each of them was doing at the same moment. If you only need numbers for each step, such as stage timings, frame rates and input latency, use --stats-path instead.

items.title: Collecting a report
items.text:
First install the model package, then launch the app through flashdreams-profile:

uv sync --package flashdreams-self-forcing
uv run flashdreams-profile -- t2v-self-forcing-wan2.1-t2v-1.3b --timeout 300 \
    --output-path artifacts/run.mp4 -- --prompt "A city street at night" --total-blocks 7

If the model takes longer to compile, increase --timeout.

The report is saved in artifacts/profiles/. To save it somewhere else, pass --report-path. By default the report records CUDA, NVTX, OS runtime and Vulkan activity; to record something different, pass --trace.

To time each stage, --stats-path (or FLASHDREAMS_SYNC_AND_PROFILE=1) makes the CPU wait for the GPU twice per step. This adds a slight delay to each step, so the timeline differs slightly from a normal run.

items.title: Reading the report
items.text:
To read the report, open the .nsys-rep file in the Nsight Systems GUI. For a quick summary in the terminal instead, run:

nsys stats --report nvtx_sum artifacts/profiles/<report>.nsys-rep

Each row of the summary is one of the ranges below, with how many times it ran and how long it took. These durations are CPU time and include waiting. For the GPU work that each range launched, use --report nvtx_gpu_proj_sum instead.

Range Meaning model.pace Waiting to hold the step rate. model.step[i] One autoregressive step. model.publish Handing the chunk to presentation. pipeline.encode / diffuse / decode Encode, denoising loop, VAE decode. pipeline.finalize KV-cache update for the next step. ui.step One UI loop iteration. input.wait From an input arriving to the first frame that shows it.

Besides these ranges, the timeline has a mark each time a frame is generated (model.frame) or shown (present.frame). Each mark includes the step that produced the frame, such as present.frame [step 5], so you can follow a frame on screen back to the step that made it.

FlashVSR and SwiftVR use their own generate method, so their reports have no pipeline.* ranges.

items.title: Using your own profiler
items.text:
A session runs with the profiler the application runner creates. To use your own, assign it at the start of init(), before registering a loop:

def init(self):
    self._profiler = MyProfiler()

The session's loops get it as self.profiler, so a model loop can record its own ranges and events:

with self.profiler.range("my_stage"):
    ...
self.profiler.event("my_event")

To profile a pipeline on its own, see Profiling a pipeline.

def __init__(self, weight: Tensor, bias: Tensor | None) -> None:
    """Initialize the transformation from existing tensors.

    Args:
        weight: Projection weight shaped ``[out_features, in_features]``.
        bias: Optional projection bias shaped ``[out_features]``.
    """
    nn.Module.__init__(self)
    self.in_features = weight.shape[1]
    self.out_features = weight.shape[0]
    self.register_buffer("weight", weight, persistent=False)
    self.register_buffer("bias", bias, persistent=False)

items.text:
rms_norm(input: Tensor, weight: Tensor, eps: float) -> Tensor

Apply RMSNorm through PyTorch's fused implementation.

The fused BF16 reduction can round differently from a decomposed module, so integrations must quality-qualify model output before enabling this path.

Source code in flashdreams/flashdreams/accelerated/common/rms_norm.py 
def rms_norm(input: Tensor, weight: Tensor, eps: float) -> Tensor:
    """Apply RMSNorm through PyTorch's fused implementation.

    The fused BF16 reduction can round differently from a decomposed module, so
    integrations must quality-qualify model output before enabling this path.
    """
    if weight.ndim != 1 or weight.shape[0] != input.shape[-1]:
        raise ValueError(
            f"RMSNorm weight {tuple(weight.shape)} does not match input "
            f"dimension {input.shape[-1]}."
        )
    return F.rms_norm(input, (input.shape[-1],), weight, eps)

Source code in flashdreams/flashdreams/accelerated/quantization/quantizer.py 
def quantize(
    original: Tensor,
    format: torch.dtype,
    granularity: Granularity,
    axis: int = -1,
    use_triton: bool = True,
) -> tuple[Tensor, Tensor]:
    """Quantize a tensor using the requested format and scale granularity.

    Args:
        original: Tensor to quantize.
        format: Data type of the quantized tensor.
        granularity: Scope over which scales are computed. ``SLICE`` reduces
            along ``axis``; ``TENSOR`` reduces over the complete tensor.
        axis: Dimension over which ``SLICE`` computes the maximum value. For a
            two-dimensional tensor, ``axis=1`` produces one scale per row and
            ``axis=0`` produces one scale per column. Defaults to ``-1``.
        use_triton: Use Triton for CUDA tensors. CPU tensors retain the Torch
            implementation. Defaults to ``True``.

    Returns:
        Quantized tensor and its FP32 scale tensor. The scale has the same
        number of dimensions as ``original`` and retains reduced dimensions
        with size one.

    Raises:
        ValueError: ``format`` or ``granularity`` is unsupported.
    """
    if format not in DTYPE_MAX:
        raise ValueError(f"unsupported quantization format: {format}")

    if granularity is Granularity.TENSOR:
        reduction_axis: int | tuple[int, ...] = tuple(range(original.ndim))
    elif granularity is Granularity.SLICE:
        reduction_axis = axis
    else:
        raise ValueError(f"unsupported quantization granularity: {granularity}")

    if use_triton and original.is_cuda:
        return quantize_triton(original, format, granularity, axis)

    original_float = original.detach().to(torch.float32)
    max_abs = original_float.abs().amax(dim=reduction_axis, keepdim=True)
    scale = (max_abs / DTYPE_MAX[format]).clamp_min(torch.finfo(torch.float32).tiny)
    quantized = (original_float / scale).clamp(-DTYPE_MAX[format], DTYPE_MAX[format])
    if not format.is_floating_point:
        quantized = quantized.round()
    return quantized.to(format), scale

Source code in flashdreams/flashdreams/accelerated/quantization/quantizer.py 
def dequantize(
    quantized: Tensor,
    *scales: Tensor,
    dtype: torch.dtype = torch.float16,
    use_triton: bool = True,
) -> Tensor:
    """Dequantize a tensor using its scale tensors.

    Args:
        quantized: Tensor to dequantize.
        scales: Scale tensors used to dequantize ``quantized``.
        dtype: Data type of the dequantized tensor. Defaults to ``torch.float16``.
        use_triton: Use Triton for CUDA tensors. CPU tensors retain the Torch
            implementation. Defaults to ``True``.

    Returns:
        Dequantized tensor in ``dtype`` after applying every scale in order.
        Without scales, casts ``quantized`` directly to ``dtype``.
    """
    if use_triton and quantized.is_cuda:
        return dequantize_triton(quantized, *scales, dtype=dtype)
    if not scales:
        return quantized.to(dtype)

    dequantized = quantized.to(scales[0].dtype)
    for scale in scales:
        dequantized = dequantized * scale
    return dequantized.to(dtype)
